title: Introduce GPU memory compactor stress runner and KV-cache consistency summarizer
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: regressions in allocator behavior and subtle KV-cache inconsistencies were observed during the November perf sweep on multi-tenant clusters. This PR adds a targeted stress runner that intentionally induces fragmentation and compaction patterns on GPUs and a complementary telemetry summarizer that validates KV-cache coherence across warmup, eviction, and re-prime cycles. Summary of changes: 1) new runner binary `gpu_mem_compactor` that (a) allocates variable-length token buffers to produce fragmentation, (b) performs controlled free/alloc cycles with configurable 'cooldown' and 'burst' phases, and (c) emits per-step allocator histograms and CUDA memory metrics; 2) a KV-cache consistency probe that performs round-trip primer->evict->reprime sequences against single- and multi-model serving stacks and records divergence rates, primer hit ratios, and rehydrate latencies; 3) a summarizer pipeline that ingests the runner output and produces a compact CSV/JSON report with per-epoch failure categories (allocation-failures, stale-lookup, rehydrate-timeouts) and heatmap-ready sparklines; 4) test harness integrations and small helpers for local reproducibility. How it works (high-level): the runner spins a configurable number of agent threads that simulate session priming with skewed length distributions, then runs a controlled eviction pattern to force allocator interaction and KV fragmentation. The KV probe injects known token sequences (deterministic primers) and validates equality of returned logits/embeddings after eviction+rehydration. The summarizer performs delta analysis per-epoch and tags results with kernel IDs and approximate GPU memory occupancy. Why this is unique: previous bench runners focused on latency shapes; this one isolates allocator and KV-cache correctness under adversarial memory patterns, making it easier to triage regressions introduced by kernel-level memory layout changes or new allocator heuristics. How to run locally: `bazel run //benchmark-lab/runners:gpu_mem_compactor -- --agents 16 --burst-ms 250 --cooldown-ms 800 --kvcache-check true --out /tmp/gpu-compact-run.json` and then `python3 tools/summarize_kv.py /tmp/gpu-compact-run.json --out /tmp/kv-summary.csv`. Testing and results: ran overnight on a p3.8xlarge equivalent; baseline run shows 0.6% KV divergence and 1.3% allocation backpressure at 95th percentile; after two iteration fixes the divergence drops to 0.02%. Related linear tasks: ENG-1289 (investigate allocator regressions), ENG-1302 (kvcache evictions triage).
